concepts.title: Animal Cell Culture Media and Serum

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Animal Cell Culture Media and Serum' refers to.
questions.a: Animal cells drink a broth of amino acids, glucose, salts, vitamins, hormones and serum, the fetal bovine kind being favourite; natural media of plasma and embryo extract reproducibility poorly, synthetic formulations run from serum-containing through serum-free and xeno-free to protein-free and chemically defined salt solutions, and serum itself both feeds and fouls - growth factors and adhesion proteins on one side, batch variability, contaminants and purification headaches on the other.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Animal Cell Culture Media and Serum'.
questions.a: Serum feeds attachment and growth but carries variability and contamination - synthetic serum-free recipes trade convenience for control.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Animal Cell Culture Media and Serum' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Laminar Hoods and CO2 Incubators' refers to.
questions.a: Aseptic work happens inside laminar flow cabinets where pre-filters and HEPA filtration wash the bench in sterile air - vertical downflow protecting the operator better than horizontal crossflow - while carbon dioxide incubators hold 37 degrees, five to ten percent carbon dioxide and about 95 percent humidity, and an inverted phase-contrast microscope watches morphology, blebbing and early contamination daily.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Laminar Hoods and CO2 Incubators'.
questions.a: Filtered airflow guards the culture from you, and the incubator guards it from the world - check both every day.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Laminar Hoods and CO2 Incubators' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Primary Secondary Finite and Continuous Cell Lines

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Primary Secondary Finite and Continuous Cell Lines' refers to.
questions.a: Cells taken straight from tissue form primary cultures of mixed, parent-like cells; passaging them builds secondary lines where the fastest growers dominate, and lifespan splits the lineage - finite lines senesce after limited divisions while transformed cells immortalise into continuous lines that grow densely, loosely and even in suspension, as HeLa cells have done since George Gey cultured them from Henrietta Lacks in 1951.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Primary Secondary Finite and Continuous Cell Lines'.
questions.a: Fresh tissue gives finite, faithful cultures; transformation buys immortality at the price of tumorigenic change.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Primary Secondary Finite and Continuous Cell Lines' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Cell Viability by Dye Exclusion and MTT

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cell Viability by Dye Exclusion and MTT' refers to.
questions.a: Counting the living drives toxicology and drug testing through two assays: dye exclusion lets trypan blue, propidium iodide or 7-AAD slip only into membrane-broken dead cells, and metabolic assays such as MTT ask live mitochondria to reduce a yellow tetrazolium salt into purple formazan whose dissolved colour scales with the number of surviving cells.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cell Viability by Dye Exclusion and MTT'.
questions.a: Dead cells leak dye in; live cells turn MTT purple - either signal reads out viability.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Cell Viability by Dye Exclusion and MTT' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Pharmaceutical Proteins from CHO Cell Culture

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Pharmaceutical Proteins from CHO Cell Culture' refers to.
questions.a: Chinese hamster ovary cells manufacture a pharmacy of human proteins - erythropoietin for anaemia, factors VIII and IX for haemophilia, tissue plasminogen activator for strokes as the first drug ever made in mammalian culture, follicle-stimulating hormone, growth hormone and interleukin-2 - while hybridoma-derived monoclonals from the transplant drug OKT3 to the HER2-blocking trastuzumab treat cancer and autoimmune disease.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Pharmaceutical Proteins from CHO Cell Culture'.
questions.a: One cell line, many medicines - CHO bioreactors and hybridomas now supply clotting factors, hormones and targeted antibodies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Pharmaceutical Proteins from CHO Cell Culture' taught, and from which source text?
